claim_scope: Closed static topology, host authority, build, staging, service, normalized-render, and evidence contracts. This proves fail-closed policy behavior only; no Docker build, Compose render, container, PostgreSQL, migration, or runner behavior was executed or verified.
architecture_decisions: The host CLI is the control plane and the only Docker API consumer; no control container exists.
Platform validation may use only baked-in synthetic probes and can claim only topology behavior.
Workflow execution requires an exact MATCH approval and rechecks it before staging, after staging, and before every runner.
Derived images are copy-only, offline builds from exact locked images, with exact local image IDs and pull_policy never.
Repository content is never mounted. The host stages bounded inputs outside repository and forbidden roots, read-only to runners, with distinct output custody.
The sole Compose network is internal and non-external; no service publishes a port or receives a Docker socket, secret, host network, broad mount, privilege, or retained capability.

checks.result: Two closed Draft 2020-12 topology schemas have stable repository-controlled identities and pass the dependency-free supported-keyword linter.
The topology contract, schemas, normalized render, mutation set, and exact image lock are bound by SHA-256 in the topology file lock.
Only the host CLI may consume the Docker API; direct Compose claims are INVALID and repository approval mutation is denied.
Workflow execution requires exact approval MATCH and fixed rechecks; platform validation cannot ingest repository input or make workflow claims.
The exact Dockerfile frontend and build contexts are frozen; RUN, remote ADD, network, secret and SSH mounts, online resolution, mutable pull behavior, and unlocked bases are denied.
Database, migration, Python, and Node identities require numeric non-root users, read-only roots, no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL, no published ports, and only the internal data network.
Repository mounts and link-like inputs are denied; staged inputs are read-only and bounded to 4096 files and 256 MiB.
PASS, FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE, and INVALID remain distinct from queued, running, completed, cancelled, failed, stale, and superseded lifecycle states; static renders and tests are not runtime proof.
All 12 authority, network, root-user, privilege, mount, build-network, evidence-collapse, published-port, external-network, and capability mutations failed with the expected stable error code.
The frozen four-schema machine-contract validator remained PASS after its schema set was made explicit.
All 74 JSON documents and 17 JSONL records parsed; the bounded credential and private-key pattern scan returned no match.
No IncidentSeal-labeled or IncidentSeal-named container exists; no image, build, Compose project, service, database, migration, or runner was started in this unit.

retained_attempts.note: The first wrapper used the unsupported Windows PowerShell ConvertFrom-Json -Depth option and exited before observable results. Split commands without that option then parsed all JSON and JSONL records, scanned for credentials, and inspected Docker container history successfully.
The read-only invocation used an unknown argument and returned stable usage failure. It did not inspect or alter approval state.
The corrected command shape still omitted the machine-output flag and failed closed. It did not inspect or alter approval state.
